question: Should OpenClaw core adopt this private, env-gated recovery restore and Gateway-admission lifecycle now, or should the portable-host contract remain outside core until its lifecycle and ownership model are approved?
rationale: The branch intentionally creates new hidden CLI, persisted recovery, and Gateway lifecycle behavior, while its own description asks reviewers to accept the ownership split and fail-closed policy; that boundary cannot be selected safely from code review alone.

options.title: Approve the core ownership boundary
options.body: Sponsor the RFC ownership model, then require dependency-order landing and end-to-end restore/admission proof before merge.

options.title: Keep the host lifecycle outside core for now
options.body: Pause this stacked series until a concrete host integration demonstrates why existing snapshot and plugin seams cannot carry the required contract.

options.title: Narrow the proposal
options.body: Retain only a minimal owner-approved snapshot contract and defer Gateway admission and host-facing restore orchestration to a later, separately reviewed change.

recommendation.title: Keep the host lifecycle outside core for now
recommendation.body: Pause this stacked series until a concrete host integration demonstrates why existing snapshot and plugin seams cannot carry the required contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked stacked recovery-contract series and can clarify its intended boundary, though final product acceptance requires a repository owner beyond the available history evidence.
